selection_rationale: Cand-01 directly addresses the identified gap G1 (end-to-end generate–verify–repair vs baselines), is experimentally falsifiable, feasible within the stated resource budget, and has high venue relevance for NetOps reliability/safety. The candidate leverages deterministic verifiers (e.g., Batfish-style) and measurable safety outcomes, aligning with established findings (see cited records).
unresolved_uncertainties: Verifier labeling error rates / false-negative rate on edge semantics and their impact on measured unsafe-change rates.
Representativeness of the synthesized workload vs production heterogeneity (vendor configs, topologies, rare failure modes).
Prompt- and model-version sensitivity driving observed differences rather than pipeline architecture.
Fairness and operational realism of the templated-automation baseline specification and fallbacks.
Data provenance, anonymization, and legal/ethical constraints for any real or realistic configuration samples.
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Preregister and validate verifier labeling on a held-out human-reviewed sample; where feasible include a second verifier or manual adjudication for contested cases.
Enrich the workload with multiple topology profiles and at least some real/anonymized configuration samples or realistic corpora; document the generation and sampling procedure.
Add a prompt-sensitivity ablation (vary prompt templates and seeds) and report those results; freeze prompt templates and seeds in the preregistration.
Precisely define the templated-automation baseline behavior, fallbacks, and operator rules in the preregistration to ensure a fair comparator.
Document dataset provenance, anonymization procedures, and state legal/ethics constraints and approvals (or justify use of fully synthetic data).
